Meet The Marketing Geeks About Us Marketing Geeks Contact Us Join Us Search for: Categories: Platform: Braze Migrating to Braze: The Migration Process Migrating from another marketing automation platform to Braze presents a significant opportunity to enhance customer engagement and drive business growth. Braze, with its robust features like real-time messaging, personalization at scale, and cross-channel orchestration, empowers marketers to deliver highly customized and impactful customer experiences. However, [...] Melissa Santos March 24, 2025 10 Minutes Read Migrating from another marketing automation platform to Braze presents a significant opportunity to enhance customer engagement and drive business growth. Braze, with its robust features like real-time messaging, personalization at scale, and cross-channel orchestration, empowers marketers to deliver highly customized and impactful customer experiences. However, this transition requires careful planning and execution. It’s important to keep in mind crucial aspects such as data migration, campaign rebuilding, rigorous testing, and go-live strategies. By understanding these key considerations and following a well-defined roadmap, marketers can successfully navigate the migration to Braze and unlock its full potential. Before you dive into a migration, it’s important to define clear, measurable goals, such as increasing customer lifetime value or improving campaign conversion rates. Create a detailed roadmap outlining timelines, milestones, and the roles and responsibilities of the cross-functional team involved. This roadmap should also incorporate a comprehensive communication plan to ensure all stakeholders are informed and aligned throughout the migration process. A thorough assessment of your current data and campaign performance is crucial. Analyze existing data sources, identify data quality issues, and understand the limitations of your current platform. This analysis will inform the data migration strategy and help you identify areas for improvement within Braze. Migrating from one customer engagement platform to another requires careful planning and execution. Here are some key areas to consider as you go throughout the process. 1. Planning & Strategy The discovery and planning phase sets the foundation for a successful Braze migration. This involves a deep dive into your current marketing technology stack, data landscape, and business objectives. Begin by defining clear, measurable goals for the migration. What are you hoping to achieve with Braze? Increased customer lifetime value (CLTV)? Improved campaign performance? Enhanced customer engagement across multiple channels? Once these goals are established, create a detailed roadmap outlining the key milestones, timelines, and resource allocation for the entire migration process. This roadmap should be a living document, regularly reviewed and updated as the project progresses. A key aspect of this phase is a thorough assessment of your existing marketing technology stack. Identify any limitations or shortcomings of your current platform that Braze can address. Analyze the performance of your current campaigns, identifying areas for improvement and opportunities for optimization within Braze. Conduct a comprehensive data audit to understand the volume, quality, and structure of your customer data. This includes analyzing data sources, identifying data quality issues, and understanding data dependencies across different systems. Furthermore, assemble a cross-functional team with representatives from marketing, IT, data science, and customer success. This diverse team will bring valuable perspectives and expertise to the migration project. Establish clear communication channels and a regular cadence for team meetings to ensure everyone is aligned and informed throughout the process. This collaborative approach will foster a shared understanding of the project goals, timelines, and potential challenges, ultimately increasing the likelihood of a successful migration. By carefully considering these factors during the discovery and planning phase, you can lay the groundwork for a smooth and successful transition to Braze. This thorough preparation will ensure that the migration project stays on track, delivers the desired outcomes, and maximizes the return on investment in the new platform. 2. Data Migration and Configuration Data migration is one of the most important aspects of any marketing automation platform transition, and migrating to Braze is no exception. This process involves carefully transferring customer data, campaign history, and existing integrations from your legacy platform to Braze. Begin with a thorough data audit to understand the volume, quality, and structure of your existing customer data. This includes analyzing data sources, identifying data quality issues, and understanding data dependencies across different systems. A crucial step is creating a detailed data mapping document that outlines how fields from your legacy platforms will be mapped to their corresponding fields within Braze. This ensures data integrity and consistency during the transfer. Data cleansing is paramount. Identify and address any data inconsistencies, duplicates, or errors before migrating. This may involve deduplicating customer records, correcting inaccurate information, and standardizing data formats. Once the data is cleansed and mapped, implement a robust data migration strategy. This could involve batch uploads, incremental syncs, or utilizing data connectors to ensure a smooth and efficient transfer of information. Rigorous testing and validation procedures are essential throughout the migration process to verify data accuracy and identify any potential issues before they impact your marketing campaigns. Keep in mind that Braze SDKs are critical in collecting valuable user data within your mobile apps or websites. This data fuels personalized marketing campaigns and enhances the overall customer experience. The data process involves integrating the Braze SDK, allowing it to collect and transmit user interactions and events. This includes automatically capturing session data, device information, and push tokens. You can further enhance data collection by implementing custom events, such as app launches, purchases, or in-app actions, providing a richer understanding of user behavior. This collected data is then synchronized with the Braze platform, where it’s used to segment audiences, personalize messages, and power targeted campaigns across various channels. During the data configuration phase, your web and app developers will be heavily involved to ensure the data you need is being pushed into Braze. By carefully planning and executing the data migration process, you can ensure a smooth transition to Braze and lay the foundation for successful marketing campaigns within the new platform. 3. Journey Orchestration The journey orchestration phase involves strategically replicating existing campaign workflows within the Braze platform while leveraging its advanced features to enhance customer engagement. Begin by defining how your existing journeys can map into campaigns and canvas flows within Braze. This allows you to compare the capabilities of both platforms, identify any discrepancies, and establish a process for recreating your journeys within your new tool. Migrating orchestrations from another marketing platform to Braze’s canvas flow involves a careful translation of your existing customer journey logic. Begin by thoroughly documenting your current orchestration rules, including entry criteria, decision points, message sequences, and exit conditions. Next, map these elements to the corresponding features within Braze canvas. Utilize canvas’s drag-and-drop interface to visually construct your customer journeys, incorporating steps like entry points, decision nodes, delays, and message sends. Leverage Braze’s advanced features like real-time triggers, A/B testing, and predictive modeling to enhance your existing orchestrations and create more personalized customer experiences. Remember to thoroughly test each Canvas Flow to ensure it functions as expected and delivers the desired customer outcomes. By carefully replicating and enhancing your existing orchestrations within Braze Canvas, you can optimize customer journeys, improve engagement rates, and drive significant business growth. Furthermore, explore opportunities to create new campaigns that leverage Braze’s unique omni-channel capabilities. This may include developing in-app messaging campaigns, implementing push notifications, or utilizing SMS marketing to reach customers on their preferred channels. By strategically leveraging Braze’s advanced features and exploring new campaign possibilities, you can significantly enhance customer engagement, improve campaign performance, and drive meaningful business outcomes. 4. Testing & Validation Quality Assurance (QA) is a critical step in any platform migration, ensuring a smooth and successful transition to Braze. This involves rigorous testing to verify the functionality and accuracy of all aspects of the platform and its integrations. Unit tests are conducted to verify the functionality of individual components, such as data imports, campaign triggers, and message delivery. This ensures that each part of the system is working as expected. Integration tests are performed to ensure seamless operation with other marketing and sales tools, such as CRM systems, website analytics platforms, and advertising platforms. These tests verify that data flows correctly between Braze and these systems, and that all integrations are functioning as intended. User Acceptance Testing (UAT) is an essential step involving members of the marketing team. This allows real users to interact with the platform and provide feedback on its usability, functionality, and overall effectiveness. This ensures that the platform meets the needs of marketing and enables them to effectively execute their campaigns within Braze. Data validation is about ensuring the accuracy, completeness, and ongoing integrity of your data. This involves meticulously verifying that all customer data has been accurately migrated from your technology systems and online properties to Braze, checking for completeness, and identifying any missing or inconsistent fields. Data cleansing is crucial. This involves deduplicating customer records, correcting errors in data fields like email addresses and phone numbers, and standardizing data formats. Furthermore, ongoing validation is essential to maintain data accuracy over time. This includes monitoring data updates, identifying and resolving any emerging data quality issues, and ensuring new customer data is correctly captured and updated within Braze. By rigorously validating data at every stage, you ensure your Braze campaigns are founded on accurate and reliable information, leading to improved targeting, enhanced campaign performance, and ultimately, a stronger customer experience. Regular QA reviews should also be conducted to identify and address any emerging issues or areas for improvement. This ongoing process ensures that the platform continues to function optimally and meets the evolving needs of your business. By following these QA steps, you can minimize risks, identify and resolve issues early on, and ensure a smooth and successful transition to the new platform. 5. Go-Live & Optimization The go-live and optimization phase marks the culmination of the Braze migration project. This stage involves a phased rollout, starting with a small segment of your audience to minimize risk and allow for close monitoring. Carefully track key performance indicators (KPIs) such as open rates, click-through rates, conversion rates, and customer lifetime value to assess campaign performance. Continuously analyze campaign performance data to identify areas for improvement. Conduct A/B testing to optimize messaging, creative elements, and campaign timing. Leverage Braze’s robust analytics and reporting features to gain deeper insights into customer behavior and identify opportunities for personalization. This data-driven approach will enable you to refine your campaigns, improve engagement rates, and ultimately achieve your marketing goals. The go-live phase is not the end of the journey. Continuous optimization is crucial for maximizing the return on your investment in Braze. Regularly review and refine your campaigns based on performance data, leverage new features as they become available, and adapt your strategies to evolving customer expectations. By embracing a culture of continuous improvement and leveraging the power of Braze’s platform, you can achieve long-term success and drive significant business growth. 6. Key Considerations Several key considerations must be addressed during a Braze migration to ensure a smooth and successful transition. Effective change management is paramount. Clearly communicate the benefits of the migration to all stakeholders, address any concerns or resistance to change proactively, and foster a culture of support and collaboration. Organizational readiness is crucial. Assess the team’s technical skills and identify any necessary training needs. Ensure that the marketing team has the necessary resources, tools, and support to effectively utilize Braze. Establish clear roles and responsibilities within the team to ensure efficient collaboration and accountability throughout the migration process. Governance is essential for long-term success. Establish clear guidelines for data usage, campaign development, and performance measurement. Implement data security and privacy measures to comply with relevant regulations. Regularly review and update these guidelines to ensure they align with evolving business needs and industry best practices. Finally, comprehensive training is vital for maximizing the return on your Braze investment. Provide comprehensive training to the marketing team on all aspects of the platform, including data management, campaign creation, analytics, and reporting. Offer ongoing support and resources, such as knowledge bases, webinars, and dedicated support channels, to ensure the team can effectively utilize Braze’s capabilities and address any challenges that may arise. By carefully considering these key considerations and implementing appropriate strategies, organizations can successfully navigate the Braze migration process and unlock the full potential of this powerful marketing platform. Are you considering a migration to Braze? If so, give Relationship One a call. We will guide you through every step, from strategic planning and data architecture design to customer journey orchestration and optimization.
